title: Character Animations and Rigging
author: seele1986
selftext:
Team,

Been using Astra and Sol to build my character animations and rigging a game I am making in Unity.  Been struggling tremendously.  I have some unique and complex use cases - much more complex than a capsule that walks around and jumps, like everyone's first demo.  It CANNOT seem to get any form of lifelike animation.  I send it photos, or videos, of say a mountain climber, to work on a climbing animation.  After a shit ton of compute and multiple iterations, the character looks like a gecko scampering up a ledge.

Are any of the other AI models, like Claude or Opus or whatever, better at character animations, joints, and rigging, than Astra/Sol?  Maybe I need to switch models to get this done?  Anyone have any advice or suggestions?

Thanks,

Seele

comments.author: PositiveScarcity8909
comments.body: Yeah due to the nature of AI for specific cases you gotta do it manual I think.

replies.author: seele1986
replies.body: Yeah it doesn’t seem to be up to par yet.

comments.author: kokutouchichi
comments.body: I mean it will get there eventually not yet though. But if you're spending money burning tokens why not just buy an animation pack on an asset store it's gotta be cheaper than blowing all your tokens and time on a simple climbing animation. And you support 3D artists.

replies.author: seele1986
replies.body: I have a couple of “never been done’s” in my game, so a lot of those animation packs won’t work too well, TBH.  I might consider it just to have a good “base” of actual good movements, though.

comments.author: zenmatrix83
comments.body:
how are ou having it process the image? its not pefect but have it create a panel of frames from beginning to end and have it compare to a video. You'll still get some wierd animations, sometimes it might be better to just go to mixamo and download a fbx and have the ai extract the motion data from it

https://preview.redd.it/q1l5botft7vh1.png?width=1792&format=png&auto=webp&s=3e3ef0f40c318ab464aaab608d43b5361ddbbfe9

replies.author: seele1986
replies.body:
So this is something I haven’t done.  Tried to explain through text what I need it to do, and I’m having terrible results.  It is obnoxious to write a couple paragraphs on how a climber climbs a rock ledge.  

I have tried mixamo, and some of them work ok, but when you get Astra or Sol to stitch in non-mixamo into the mixamo animations, then add hysteresis, inverse kinematics, and guns and tools and stuff, it seems to break down.

replies.author: zenmatrix83
replies.body: I do a combination of this and the ask the ai to create descriptions of the images to figure out how it’s interpreting them. Also having it do different filter and passes of white frame clay normals face direction helps. One of mine have an xyz gizmo to help keep things oriented properly

comments.author: Fuzzzy420
comments.body:
What software? 
I use blender for asset creation, rigging and animation and get great results with sol6.1 and opus 5.5 
I use blender autorig pro as well. 

It takes forever but looks good.

replies.author: seele1986
replies.body: I know my dot can use blender on its virtual computer, and Astra/Sol can use blender on my computer, but I suck with blender.  Wondering if I need to change the prompts from “fix this in the game” to “go into blender and animate and rig, then we review, THEN we import into the game”.  Could this struggle be a workflow issue on my end?

replies.author: Fuzzzy420
replies.body:
Yes. 
And I would guess that ai can handle animations better in blender then doing it in engine. Blender python code works as well as mcp. Just try it

replies.author: seele1986
replies.body: Good to know - may need to try it out!

comments.author: Nilo_Team
comments.body: yeah LLMs really aren't animators yet lol. what's worked better for us is video to animation on nilo.io, you film the climb and it maps it onto the rigged char. not perfect for weird custom moves tho

comments.author: Sorry-Version6112
comments.body:
The best way is to use Mixamo. It's free and really good.   
Also, there's a claude mcp for blender. I haven't used it, but I have heard great things about it. Do let me know how it works for you.
